allowed_localisation: The qualification named (DE: 1.3 Abi / Bachelor; FR: bac+5 / Master; ES: Grado / Máster / nota media alta)

The type of employer or job (DE: EDEKA/Rewe summer job or cashier; FR: caissière at Carrefour/Leclerc; ES: cajera/reponedor at Mercadona/Carrefour). Real brand names only as the place of rejection, never implying wrongdoing
The creator's situation (student looking for a summer job vs. unemployed graduate)
Who gave the HR hint (friend, cousin, former HR colleague)
Local slang, emoji and the wording of the POV text
The CV language and the template or field chosen (finance, admin, retail, etc.)
The exact score numbers, as long as they are what the product really shows
How long it takes for the rejection to arrive (minutes / same day)
beats: 1. HOOK: POV on-screen text ('POV: rejected as a cashier' / 'Rejected at EDEKA with a 1.3 Abi 🤡'). Creator says they are job-hunting and just got rejected for a simple job, adds 'not that I have anything against this job', then names their high qualification.
2. SUSPICION: the rejections arrive within minutes of applying. They asked a friend who used to work in HR.
3. REVEAL: the friend says the CV is not getting through the automated applicant filters. The creator says 'so they never even saw my CV, and yes, they really didn't'.
4. PRODUCT IN: 'So here I'm uploading my CV to Parakeet AI, a site that was recommended to me.' Screen recording of the CV upload.
5. BAD SCORE: Parakeet AI analyses the CV and gives a score. It's not great, and the creator explains it's a Canva-style CV with lots of icons.
6. REWRITE: the AI reworks and optimises the CV very quickly and asks questions in the chat.
7. TEMPLATE: the creator picks a clean template suited to their field (the original's 'finance' format), and the CV is rebuilt in it.
8. TAILOR: the creator pastes the job ad (link or text) so the AI tailors the CV to the posting, 'to have a better chance of being picked'.
9. CHAT: the creator answers the AI's questions and accepts or edits its suggestions (replaces the JobStep assistant 'Lia').
10. RESULT: the new, much higher score is shown on screen, and the final optimised CV is scrolled through with 'so yeah, much better chances now'.
X08.filming: About 45–60 s, vertical 9:16, one take or loosely cut, phone selfie at home with natural light, casual and unpolished. Beats 1–3: talking head with the POV text overlay for the first 3 s. Beats 4–10: screen recording of Parakeet AI with the creator's voice-over (face in a small overlay or green screen is optional). Demo order: upload CV → score/analysis (low) → AI rewrite + questions in chat → choose template → paste job ad to tailor → answer in chat / edit → new score + final CV scroll. Subtitles burned in, no music or only quiet music.
X08.hook: On-screen POV text plus a deadpan, slightly exasperated line to camera: the creator got rejected for a basic, low-barrier job (summer job at a supermarket or cashier) even though they have a top qualification (e.g. 1.3 Abitur / bac+5). Example title: 'Mit 1.3 Abi bei EDEKA abgelehnt.... 🤡'
not_allowed: Adding a CTA, discount code, link-in-bio push or a spoken URL (that would make it an ad format)
Introducing the product before the rejection story and the filter reveal (beats 1–3 must come first)
Turning it into a step-by-step tutorial or listicle, or dropping the outrage or irony hook
Showing or mentioning features Parakeet AI does not have: an application overview or tracker, a 'New job' button, cover letters, or a named assistant like 'Lia'
Calling it JobStep or keeping any JobStep UI or wording
Claiming the CV is guaranteed to pass applicant filters, or guaranteeing interviews or a job
Showing a made-up score (e.g. a fixed '96%') that the product didn't actually produce, or calling it an official 'ATS score' unless the UI labels it that way
Saying the employer (EDEKA etc.) uses a specific filter software or acted unfairly or illegally
Presenting the HR friend's hint as verified fact about that specific employer. It stays a personal anecdote ('she told me it's probably…')
Implying Parakeet AI sends applications or contacts employers
X08.premise: An overqualified creator vents about being rejected for an entry-level job and says they have nothing against the job itself. They find out from someone with HR experience that their CV was probably never seen by a person because it did not get past automated filters. They then fix the CV on screen with Parakeet AI's Resume Maker, going from a weak score to a strong one. The tone is ironic disbelief that turns into a practical fix. It is one personal anecdote, not a tutorial.

features_used: Paste a job ad (link or text) to tailor the CV
AI rewrites/tailors the CV to the job
product.spoken_brand: Beat 4, said once in passing ('I'm uploading my CV to Parakeet AI, a site that was recommended to me'). The brand may also appear on screen during the demo. No URL is spoken.

X08.title_en: Rejected for a simple job despite top grades 🤡: the CV never got past the filter
